record.original_question: Prove that a simple(that is, without proper non-trivial connected normal subgroups) algebraic group M over an algebraically closed field cannot act definably, faithfully, and irreducibly on a simple group of finite Morley rank other than M/Z(M).

evidence.quote: Prove that a simple(that is, without proper non-trivial connected normal subgroups) algebraic group M over an algebraically closed field cannot act definably, faithfully, and irreducibly on a simple group of finite Morley rank other than M/Z(M).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and let $M$ be a simple algebraic group over $K$, where "simple" means that $M$ is connected and has no proper non-trivial connected normal algebraic subgroups. Let $Z(M)$ denote the center of $M$.

Recall that a group $N$ is said to be of finite Morley rank if there is a Morley rank function on the definable subsets of $N$ (in some structure in which $N$ is interpretable) taking finite values, and $N$ is called simple if it has no proper non-trivial normal subgroups. An action of $M$ on $N$ by group automorphisms is called definable if the action map $M \times N \to N$ is definable, faithful if its kernel is trivial, and irreducible if $N$ has no proper non-trivial $M$-invariant definable subgroups.

Prove that if $M$ acts definably, faithfully, and irreducibly on a simple group $N$ of finite Morley rank, then $N \cong M/Z(M)$.
